topomer.note: 63 of 76 molecules can be cut at the framework

findings.text: 15 chemotype(s); the largest holds 44 of 76 molecules -- a series of several scaffolds has no common frame, and an alignment will invent one
the common framework (framework of the largest chemotype) has 6 heavy atoms, about 24% of a typical molecule, and 83% of the set can be cut at it

the 6 shared framework atoms sit 9.0 A apart between molecules, over the best of their matches (67 of 76 carry them); but that framework is only 24% of a typical molecule and matches it 12 ways on average, so this cannot say whether the set shares a frame -- look at it
the aligned model is +0.208 in q2 against counts (95% interval -0.040 to +0.543) -- the frame buys nothing over counts
the aligned model is +0.083 in q2 against invariant (95% interval -0.122 to +0.347) -- the frame buys nothing over invariant
the aligned model is -0.114 in q2 against topomer (95% interval -0.512 to +0.173) -- cutting the molecules and posing the pieces by rule does as well as the frame, on the molecules that can be cut
the aligned model is +0.205 in q2 against descriptors (95% interval +0.056 to +0.373) -- the geometry earns its place

why: the frame carries signal and the molecules are superimposed, so a frame exists whoever made it; the several Murcko scaffolds only mean the program could not have built it, not that it is wrong
